problem: Existing VLN-CE agents lack sufficient navigation knowledge and struggle with obstacle avoidance in continuous environments, so LLM-based planners produce imprecise plans and get stuck in complex scenes.
motivation: LLMs offer strong reasoning for instruction following but lack domain-specific navigation knowledge, and continuous-environment navigation needs robust collision handling. Retrieval-augmented generation can inject navigation knowledge, and prompt-based feedback can help with obstacle avoidance.
key_idea: Build a navigation knowledge base and use RAG to enrich the LLM's input for planning (RAGNav), plus a Prompt Enhanced Obstacle Avoidance (PEOA) strategy to handle obstacles.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract claims that knowledge retrieval improves plan precision and that prompt-based obstacle avoidance improves robustness, giving gains of 2% SR on R2R-CE and 2.32% SR on RxR-CE.
method: Navigation knowledge base: constructed to store navigation-related knowledge for retrieval.
RAG-enhanced LLM input: retrieves relevant knowledge and adds it to the LLM prompt to generate more precise navigation plans.
PEOA (Prompt Enhanced Obstacle Avoidance): prompt-based strategy that improves flexibility and robustness of the agent in complex environments and around obstacles.

setting.backbone: LLM with RAG (specific model not stated in abstract)

numbers_note: abstract only; the abstract reports only relative SR gains (+2% on R2R-CE, +2.32% on RxR-CE), with no absolute values or splits.
results: The abstract states that RAGNav increases navigation accuracy and obstacle avoidance, with SR improvements of 2% on R2R-CE and 2.32% on RxR-CE. The baseline these are measured against is not specified.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so the evaluation details, baselines and absolute numbers are unknown.
